questions.q: Displacement of a wave is expressed as $x(t)=5 \cos \left(628 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) m$. The wavelength of the wave when its velocity is $300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{t})=5 \cos \left[628 \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{2}\right] \mathrm{m} \\ & \text { velocity }\left(\mathrm{v}_\omega\right)=300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{w}}=\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{K}} \\ & 300=\frac{628}{\mathrm{~K}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~K}=\frac{628}{300} \\ & \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}=\frac{628}{300} \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{2 \times 3.14 \times 300}{628} \\ & \lambda=2 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The equations of two waves are given by :

${y}_{1} = 5\sin 2\pi\left(x - vt\right)cm$

${y}_{2} = 3\sin 2\pi\left(x - vt + 1 . 5\right)cm$

These waves are simultaneously passing through a string. The amplitude of the resulting wave is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given equations can be written as,

${y}_{1} = 5\sin \left(2\pix - 2\pivt\right)cm$~and

${y}_{2} = 3\sin \left(2\pix - 2\pivt + 3\pi\right)cm$

From the given equations we can conclude that the phase difference between the waves is~$3\pi$~i.e. odd multiple of $\pi$. Therefore, destructive interference will happen.

$A = \left|{A}_{1} - {A}_{2}\right| = 2cm$

questions.q: The ratio of speed of sound in hydrogen gas to the speed of sound in oxygen gas at the same temperature is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the speed of sound in hydrogen gas is given by

${v}_{H2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gammaRT}{M{H}_{2}}} . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the speed of sound in oxygen is given by

${v}_{O2} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{\gammaRT}{M{O}_{2}}} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (1) by (2) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

\dfrac{v{H}_{2}}{v{O}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M{O}_{2}}{M{H}_{2}}} . . . \left(3\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{v{H}_{2}}{v{O}_{2}}& = & \sqrt{\dfrac{32}{2}}\\ & = & 4: 1\end{cases}

$

$⇒ {T}_{X} / {T}_{Z} = 9 / 4 = 2 . 25$

questions.q: A small speaker delivers $2W$ of audio output. At what distance from the speaker will one detect $120dB$ intensity sound? [Given reference intensity~of sound as ${10}^{- 12}W / m^{2}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the intensity of sound hear by observer is $I$
$120 = 10\log_{10} \dfrac{I}{{10}^{- 12}}$
$12 = log I - \log_{10} {10}^{- 12}$
$= log I + 12$
$log I = 0 ⇒ I = 1\dfrac{watt}{m^{2}}$
$I = \dfrac{P}{4\pir^{2}}$
$⇒ 1 = \dfrac{2}{4\pir^{2}} ⇒ r = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} = 0.4m = 40cm$

questions.q: Two light beams of intensities in the ratio of $9: 4$& are allowed to interfere. The ratio of the intensity of maxima and minima will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Data provided in the question is, the ratio of the intensities,

$\dfrac{I1}{I2} = \dfrac{9}{4}$

After taking square root of above equation on both sides, we get,

~$\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Apply componendo and dividendo,
$⇒ \dfrac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}} = \dfrac{3 + 2}{3 - 2} = \dfrac{5}{1}$
$⇒ \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}\right)2 = \dfrac{Imax}{Imin} = \dfrac{25}{1}$

questions.q: A radar sends an electromagnetic signal of electric field \left({E}_{0}\right) = 2 . 25Vm^{- 1}$ and magnetic field \left({B}_{0}\right) = 1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 8}T$ which strikes a target on line of sight at a distance of $3$ km in a medium. After that, a part of signal (echo) reflects back towards the radar with same velocity and by same path. If the signal was transmitted at time $t = 0$& from radar, then after how much time echo will reach to the radar?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The speed of light is given by,

$c = \dfrac{E0}{B0} = \dfrac{2 . 25}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 8}} = 1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

Therefore, time taken for~the echo will be,

$t = \dfrac{2d}{c} = \dfrac{6 \times {10}^{3}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}} = 4 \times {10}^{- 5}s$

questions.q: A wire of length $L$ and mass per unit length $6.0 \times {10}^{- 3}kgm^{- 1}$ is put under tension of $540N .$ Two consecutive frequencies that it resonates at are: $420$ Hz and $490Hz .$ Then $L$ in meters is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fundamental frequency $= 490 - 420 = 70Hz$
$70 = \dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}}$
$⇒ 70 = \dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{540}{6 \times {10}^{- 3}}}$
$⇒ L = \dfrac{1}{2 \times 70}\sqrt{90 \times {10}^{3}} = \dfrac{300}{140}$
$⇒ L \approx 2.14m$

questions.q: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe is equal to the first overtone frequency of an open organ pipe. If length of the open pipe is $60$ cm, the length of the closed pipe will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{λ}{4} = {L}_{1}2\left(\dfrac{λ}{2}\right) = {L}_{2}$

$\text{As}, v = f\lambda ⇒ {f}_{2} = \dfrac{2v}{2{L}_{2}}$

$⇒ v = {f}_{1}\left(4{L}_{1}\right) ⇒ {f}_{2} = \dfrac{v}{L2}$

$⇒ {f}_{1} = \dfrac{v}{4{L}_{1}}$

As per question, ${f}_{1} = {f}_{2}$

$\dfrac{v}{4{L}_{1}} = \dfrac{v}{L2}$

$⇒ {L}_{2} = 4{L}_{1}$

$⇒ 60 = 4 \times {L}_{1}$

$⇒ {L}_{1} = 15cm$

questions.q: A one metre long (both ends open) organ pipe is kept in a gas that has double the density of air at STP. Assuming the speed of sound in air at STP is $300m / s,$ the frequency difference between the fundamental and second harmonic of this pipe is __________ Hz.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$V = \sqrt{\dfrac{B}{ρ}}$
$\dfrac{{V}_{pipe}}{{V}_{air}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{B}{2ρ}}}{\sqrt{\dfrac{B}{ρ}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
${V}_{pipe} = \dfrac{{V}_{air}}{\sqrt{2}}$
${f}_{n} = \dfrac{( n + 1 ) {V}_{pipe}}{2l}$
${f}_{1} - {f}_{0} = \dfrac{Vpipe}{2l} = \dfrac{300}{2\sqrt{2}} = 105.75Hz \lleft(if\sqrt{2} =1.41)$
$= 106.05Hz \lleft(if\sqrt{2} =1.414)$

questions.q: A transverse harmonic wave on a string is given by& $y \left(x, t\right) = 5\sin \left($6t + 0 . 003x\right)$~where $x$ and $y$ are in $cm$ and $t$~in $sec$. The wave~velocity is _________ $ms^{- 1}$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The general equation for a wave can be written as& $y = Asin \left(\omegat +kx\right)$. Comparing it with the given equation,~$y = 5\sin \left(6t + 0 . 003x\right)$,

$\omega =6rads^{- 1}$,~$k = 0 . 003{cm}^{- 1}$

Using the equation,~$v = \dfrac{ω}{k}$

$v = \dfrac{6}{0 . 003 \times {10}^{2}} =20ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two light beams of intensities $4I$~and $9I$ interfere on a screen. The phase difference between these beams on the screen at point $A$ is zero and at point $B$ is $\pi$. The difference of resultant intensities, at the point $A$ and $B$, will be _____~$I$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The resultant intensity is given by& ${I}_{net} = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} + 2\sqrt{{I}_{1}}\sqrt{{I}_{2}}cosϕ$

Now, for~${I}_\max$, phase angle is~$ϕ = 0$~and for~${I}_\min$,~phase angle is~$ϕ = \pi$.

Thus,~${I}_\max = \left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)2 = \left(\sqrt{9I} + \sqrt{4I}\right)2 = 25I$

And~${I}_\min = \left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)2 = \left(\sqrt{9I} - \sqrt{4I}\right)2 = I$

The difference of resultant intensities is~${I}_\max - {I}_\min = 25I - I = 24I$

questions.q: A sonometer wire of resonating length $90 \mathrm{~cm}$ has a fundamental frequency of $400 \mathrm{~Hz}$ when kept under some tension. The resonating length of the wire with fundamental frequency of $600 \mathrm{~Hz}$ under same tension _____{\mathrm{cm}}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}_0=400 \mathrm{~Hz} ; \mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mu}}=\text { constant } \\ & \frac{\lambda}{2}=\mathrm{L} ; \quad \mathrm{v}=\mathrm{f}_0 \lambda\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \mathrm{f}_0}=\mathrm{L} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=2 \mathrm{Lf}_0 \\ & \mathrm{~L}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \mathrmf^{\prime}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{Lf}_0}{2 \mathrmf^{\prime}} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{Lf}_0}{\mathrmf^{\prime}}=\frac{90 \times 400}{600}=60\end{aligned}$$
